title: Blender's UI and Runtime: Much Faster Than GPUI

author: ppmpreetham

summaryRaw: Blender's user interface, as a library you can use from Python, Rust, JavaScript (React, Svelte), C, C++ and Dear ImGui. People spent decades building and optimizing Blender's GUI. It's battery and memory efficient, and super duper fast. We decoupled it, to give everyone a chance to build their own products with it. It supports multiple languages and frameworks, so you won't miss a beat!
Website and full documentation: bui.preetham.top · Chat: Discord
This README is a small book. Read it front to back for the whole story, or jump to the chapter you need. Every chapter links to a longer guide in docs/ or on the website when there's more to say.

comments.author: munksbeer
comments.textRawHtml: Can I please congratulate you on your README. It rapidly tells me what I'm looking at, and why I might be interested in the project. There are so many READMEs around that ... just don't do that. They ramble about technical implementation details, how their language choice is amazing, and a third of the way through the README, I'm still left wondering, "but what does this project do?".

children.author: whatthejesus
children.textRawHtml:
It is ALL AI generated I can say that because I recently worked on a landing page and wrestled with Claude Opus the WHOLE way through. Claude has no idea how to write copy. Neither do any of the others, you have to edit with a fine-toothed comb.

To the project maintainer: don’t ask people to read a terrible AI generated sales pitch novella that quantifies your AI generated port against every UI framework out there.

Here’s the obvious giveaways:

“ 4. The many ways in” “ Python, four ways”

“ tkinter: all 7,846 public names of tkinter and ttk. Nine real programs behave identically on the standard library and on BUI.”

“ Rust: the web platform, natively”

Ugh it’s excruciating. You’re better off with a readme that shows a few screenshots and installation instructions.

children.author: whatthejesus
children.textRawHtml:
None of them is better than the others on the frontier. But to be honest, the models are designed for acing STEM exams not doing copywriting.

This is further evidence of the need for small models doing specific things well.

Where I would say models fit in the process is establishing the general layout of documentation and iteratively refining things out. Interestingly, it’s the same for image generation too. But 9 out of 10 it creates incomplete work that needs refinement.

Go wide, then hone in, refine. There’s no such thing as getting AI to single shot creative tasks. Which is funny because everyone thought writers are on the chopping block initially, but that is unequivocally NOT the case.

Even technical tasks, agents doing it their own way yields garbage in some right. It’s just a question of how long it runs before it goes down a path of no return.

Human in the loop is the only way. And, to be honest, what’s the f*king rush anyway? We all need to slow down. Good ideas with unravel in time. :)

children.author: 0x69420
children.textRawHtml:
it's funny how these claudese constructions also come out of lil baby local qwens and stuff too. i guess they're just directly distilling a claude endpoint, or whatever.

like, if people are gonna be turning the crank to generate prose-like text from statistical models and calling it a day, aren't "subagents" a hip new thing nowadays? there do exist models that aren't overcooked to impressively bad long-tail in the pursuit of maximum coding benchmark scores. such other models generate prose-like text that is significantly less miserable to wade through.

if you're a vibecoder who's terminally committed to the bit, for god's sake, at least tell a local gemma to draft your readme or something. an occasional outright falsehood is less damaging to usability than the experience of reading feeling like trudging through a pool filled with treacle. (mind, both are a violation of trust, and a failure to deliver proof of work, and please stop, but at least if the falsehoods are comprehensible and identifiable there's light at the end of the tunnel)

children.author: meowface
children.textRawHtml:
Many of my old >1K star GitHub projects were not that great, but I always made sure to create the cleanest, simplest possible READMEs, inspired by things like the Python requests library's docs (https://github.com/psf/requests). I think it helped a lot in their success.

I remember someone once created a GitHub issue requesting I turn the README into some verbose technical thing with full API docs and a bunch of people replied saying they greatly preferred the "pitch + high-level examples" style.
